title: Field accumulator compact notes and patch candidates (Apr 2026)
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, field-oriented synthesis of recent customer signals (Mar 24 — Apr 1) with concrete small-patch candidates we can ship in a 1–2 sprint window. Tone is intentionally informal: think notes-to-engineering and CS triage to accelerate low-effort, high-confidence impact.

Topline themes (short):
- Recurrent latency spikes for bursty workloads (esp. 8–30 sec tails) tied to cold KV cache misses and backend model fallbacks.
- Customers asking for clearer routing controls and per-route fallback visibility (want to know when their traffic is routed to cheaper model variant).
- Small UX/observability gaps: token-level cost attribution sometimes blurred across multi-route requests; early adopters want per-request trace ids surfaced in the console.
- A few customers experiencing embedding drift vs. earlier runs after quantized model upgrades — asks for deterministic rolling-pin option.

Representative vignettes (raw customer language):
- EduBot (PLG startup): "We see occasional 10–20s answers during peak school hours. It kills our synchronous classroom workflow. We can tolerate slightly higher average latency if tails disappear."
- LegalMate (enterprise): "Our privacy bar requires Private deployment, but we still want alerts when routing falls back to lower-tier model variants — our SLA depends on model parity."
- MarketplaceX (scale SaaS): "Embedding vectors look subtly different after the 'smaller' quant release — clustering drifted. We need a way to pin the older vector shape while we test."

Quantified heuristic impact estimates (back-of-envelope):
- Tail-latency reductions from proactive KV prewarm: 30–60% reduction in 95/99p; customer impact: reduces perceived failure + lower retries. Effort: ~3 engineer days for a first pass (runtime + small config UI).
- Per-route fallback visibility in Console: medium customer confidence uplift. Effort: ~5 eng days (backend event tags + UI flag).
- Per-request trace id in Console + API header: low effort (2–3 days) but high debuggability for CS.
- Deterministic pin for embeddings (version-pin rollback toggle at profile level): moderate effort (8–12 days) – non-invasive but needs QA across hosted/private modes.

Patch candidates (mini tasks we can assign, with owners and suggested acceptance criteria):
1) "kv-prewarm-lite" (owner: SRE / serving-runtime): prewarm cache on route-activation and on predictable daily windows. Acceptance: reduce 99p tail on sample workload by >=30% in lab runs; config toggle added to route JSON. Estimated: 3 days.
2) "request-trace-header" (owner: developer-experience): add "X-Redwood-Trace" header to SDKs + surface last 7 days in Console traces for individual requests. Acceptance: header present in SDKs and visible in request JSON in Console; CS can match customer traces to logs. Estimated: 2 days.
3) "fallback-note" (owner: product-hosted-api + console): show on-route timeline icon when fallback to a cheaper variant occurs and include reason (capacity/budget). Acceptance: timeline event visible; hover text explains reason; linked to incident id if fallback due to capacity. Estimated: 5 days.
4) "embedding-pin-toggle" (owner: optimize/product): route-level toggle to lock embedding model/quantization for a route for N days. Acceptance: toggle prevents automatic rollout of quantized variants; regression test ensures embedding distances stable vs baseline. Estimated: 10 days.

Low-risk quick wins (can be done by CS + small eng support):
- Add a short KB article that explains common causes of latency tails and how to configure prefix caching and batching. (owner: CS knowledge ops, 1 day)
- Build a reusable query that surfaces customers with >2s increase in median latency week-over-week (owner: observability, 1–2 days)

Open risk flags and unknowns:
- Some tail spikes may be caused by third-party infra (networking/hypervisor) not runtime; need an SRE-led signature study.
- Quantized model drift: we need to quantify what "drift" means for customers (clustering vs. semantic quality). Proposal: run a 10k-query regression harness comparing older vs new quant under customer prompts.
- Multi-tenant vs Dedicated behavior differences for KV prewarm — ensure changes don't create noise for other customers.

Suggested short-term roadmap (next 6 weeks):
Week 0–1: ship request-trace-header + KB article + observability query.
Week 2–4: kv-prewarm-lite in canary for low-impact routes; telemetry check.
Week 4–6: fallback-note in Console + enable fallback annotations for customers in pilot.
Parallel (investigate): plan regression harness for embeddings and draft spec for embedding-pin-toggle.

Suggested owners (first-pass):
- SRE/Serving runtime: kv-prewarm-lite, tail signature study
- Developer-experience: request-trace-header + SDK bumps
- Product-hosted-api + Console: fallback-note timeline UI
- Optimize/Product: embedding-pin-toggle spec + regression harness
- Customer Success: pilot customers, KB article, and escalation playbook

Acceptance and pilot plan:
- Identify 3 pilot customers (EduBot, LegalMate, MarketplaceX) for early testing.
- Track: latency p50/p95/p99, number of fallbacks, embedding distance drift metric (cosine similarity delta).
- Timeboxed pilot: 2 weeks per patch; roll back if negative signal.

Immediate asks for this week (what I need from you):
- Engineering: quick thumbs up on estimates for kv-prewarm-lite and request-trace-header (Marcus).
- Product/Console: confirm whether fallback events can be surfaced as an existing event type or we need a new event schema (Anjali).
- CS: confirm pilot willingness from EduBot / LegalMate (Sofia).

Notes to self / unresolved items:
- Need to link to telemetry discovery ticket (Linear CS-490) in the next update.
- Check whether Dedicated customers already have a similar prewarm mechanism in their infra.

Appendix: raw signal snippets (copied from support threads, lightly redacted):
- "classroom latency spikes at 11am PT — students waiting 15s sometimes, we have to fallback to async" — EduBot support thread 2026-03-28
- "Noted that embedding clusters diverged after the April quant push" — MarketplaceX, slack thread thread_ts:1650000025.000300
- "We were routed to 'gpt-lite' today without notice and noticed shorter answers" — LegalMate, ticket #LM-1122

If anything here looks off or you want a separate, fully-formed PRD for the embedding pin feature, say the word and I'll draft it (this doc is intentionally minimal so we can move fast).

-- Marcus (CS)
